U.S. stocks fell, and Treasury yields rose, on Tuesday.
Credit: Angela Weiss / AFP via Getty Images

The major stock indexes appeared on track to recoup some of their recent losses this morning, with futures tied to the Nasdaq 100, Dow Jones and S&P 500 all pointing upward; AI-related stocks were rising after CoreWeave handed in strong quarterly results; Nvidia shares were rising premarket after a tough start to the week; the yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note remained elevated amid anticipation of a rate hike in December; and OpenAI's revenue reportedly grew 50% over the past quarter.

Here's what you need to know today.

Stocks Look Poised to Rise

Happy Veterans Day; stock markets are open today, though bond markets are closed.

Futures tied to the Nasdaq 100 were recently up 1.8%, those tied to the S&P 500 up 0.9% and those associated with the Dow were 0.2% higher. All three indexes finished Tuesday down after an inflation reading strengthened expectations for an interest rate hike. Read our full coverage of today's trading here.

Oil prices were starting to reverse recent declines. The global benchmark, Brent Crude, was recently up 1.2% to a bit less than $93 a barrel. The price of gold was rising, recently at around $4,050 per ounce. Bitcoin was sliding, changing hands below $74,000, according to CoinDesk.

Tech Shares Rise, CoreWeave Stock Climbs

Shares of CoreWeave (CRWV) were rising after the company handed in better-than-expected results on Tuesday night. The AI cloud provider reported nearly $3.7 billion in revenue and $709 million in losses, both of which came in ahead of estimates compiled by Visible Alpha. CEO Michael Intrator called it a "breakout quarter" and raised CoreWeave's full-year revenue forecast to $13.3 billion. CoreWeave shares were recently up about 15% premarket.

Those numbers fanned confidence in the broader AI trade. Applied Digital (APLD) and Lumentum Holdings (LITE) were up almost 10% in early morning trading. The Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) was up about 8%, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) was up more than 5%.

Nvidia Shares on Track to Rise

Nvidia (NVDA) shares were gaining ground after dropping 10% over the past two days, with the stock recently up nearly 4% premarket. Investors ditched shares of the chip giant after learning this weekend that CEO Jensen Huang is under investigation for reportedly having an affair with a Chinese spy; broader softness in tech shares has also been a weight on the shares, with recent bearishness sparked by widespread anticipation of an interest-rate hike next month. (More on that next.) The company is set to address investors next week when it hands in its third-quarter results.

US stock index futures advanced on Wednesday, indicating a higher opening on Wall Street following declines in the previous session, as quarterly results from cloud computing provider CoreWeave supported technology shares.

Nasdaq 100 futures increased 1.9%, reflecting gains in technology-related stocks after CoreWeave reported third-quarter results above analyst expectations and raised its full-year revenue guidance.

The anticipated market advance followed Tuesday's losses, when stronger-than-expected US inflation data contributed to expectations of further interest rate increases by the Federal Reserve.

CoreWeave Shares Advance Following Quarterly Results

The company's earnings announcement coincided with a 1.9% increase in Nasdaq 100 futures, indicating expectations of a higher opening for technology shares.

The supplied report did not provide specific revenue or earnings figures from CoreWeave's quarterly announcement.

Nvidia Shares Gain 3.7% in Premarket Trading

The semiconductor company is a major supplier of processors used in artificial intelligence computing infrastructure.

Its share price movement contributed to the technology sector's anticipated recovery following Tuesday's market decline.

Wall Street's major equity indices finished lower on Tuesday after the US Labor Department reported that consumer prices increased more than economists had expected in October.

Wall Street's financing scare around AI cloud providers is easing after a strong quarter from CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV). CoreWeave stock is at $56.35, up 16% in morning trading. The company reported Q3 2026 results after the close on November 10, beating revenue estimates and raising its 2026 revenue and adjusted operating income guidance.

simonkr / Getty Images

CoreWeave's results helped lift tech and chip stocks, including NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA). They also pushed NASDAQ 100 futures higher in a rebound from tech losses on November 10. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, meanwhile, called the latest inflation report "borderline disturbing" as the Fed considers more rate hikes.

CoreWeave's Breakout Quarter Answers the Financing Scare

Neoclouds came under scrutiny this month as investors questioned the durability of the AI trade. CNBC reported that CoreWeave's credit default swap (CDS) spreads had widened past 11% earlier this month, a level generally viewed as distress. That background made the quarterly report a funding test.

On November 10, CoreWeave disclosed Q3 revenue of $3.66 billion, up 168% year over year (YoY), ahead of the $3.54 billion consensus estimate from Fiscal.ai. Backlog at CoreWeave reached $132.5 billion, up 138% YoY. Revenue guidance for 2026 at CoreWeave rose to $13 billion to $13.3 billion, above the $12.86 billion LSEG analysts expected. Adjusted operating income guidance at CoreWeave climbed to $1.275 billion to $1.375 billion, exceeding the $1.07 billion Visible Alpha projected.

US stock futures advanced on Wednesday as stronger-than-expected quarterly results from CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) supported technology shares, while investors assessed reports of rising revenue at OpenAI (NASDAQ:OAI) and a potentially higher initial public offering valuation for Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT).

The gains came despite volatility in government bond markets following US inflation data and comments from Federal Reserve officials that increased expectations of further interest-rate increases.

At 03:04 ET, S&P 500 futures were up 48 points, or 0.6%, while Nasdaq 100 futures gained 412 points, or 1.5%. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures increased 102 points, or 0.2%.

Technology Futures Recover Following Wall Street Declines

US equity futures moved higher after the major Wall Street indices declined during the previous session.

Technology stocks had experienced substantial fluctuations in recent trading sessions as investors evaluated the potential impact of increased regulatory scrutiny of artificial intelligence following the US midterm elections.

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) remained under pressure following reports concerning Chief Executive Jensen Huang's alleged personal relationship with an individual suspected of links to Chinese intelligence. The allegations remain unverified in the supplied reporting.

Meanwhile, developments involving CoreWeave, Anthropic and OpenAI contributed to renewed attention on investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure and services.

The recovery in technology-related futures also followed gains in several international equity markets, although government bond prices declined in Japan, Australia and other markets.

US Treasury trading was scheduled to remain closed on Wednesday for Veterans Day.

CoreWeave Reports $3.66 Billion in Quarterly Revenue and Raises Market Expectations

CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, exceeding analyst forecasts as demand for cloud computing services used in artificial intelligence applications continued.

The company also recorded a loss of $1.27 per share, which was smaller than market expectations.

CoreWeave provided full-year revenue guidance of $13 billion to $13.3 billion, above Wall Street estimates.

Chief Executive Michael Intrator described the reporting period as a "breakout quarter."

The company's shares increased by more than 18% in extended trading following the announcement.

The results followed a period of substantial share price volatility, during which CoreWeave had lost more than 40% of its market value over the preceding month.

Investing.com - Futures linked to the main U.S. stock indices rise, as investor sentiment around artificial intelligence brightens following upbeat guidance from neocloud player CoreWeave, although bets on Federal Reserve interest rate hikes rattle global bond markets. Anthropic's bankers are reportedly eyeing an increase to the Claude maker's initial public offering valuation, while OpenAI's third-quarter revenue is said to have spiked.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 10% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

1. Futures rise

U.S. stock futures ticked higher on Wednesday. By 03:04 ET (08:04 GMT), the S&P 500 futures contract had climbed by 48 points, or 0.6%, Nasdaq 100 futures had gained 412 points, or 1.5%, and Dow futures had inched up by 102 points, or 0.2%.

The main averages on Wall Street retreated in the prior session, despite renewed enthusiasm around AI. Stocks in the sector gyrated sharply last week, with AI names rebounding after a steep selloff driven by fears of stricter political oversight of the technology after the U.S. midterm elections.

Optimism around AI was resilient in the face of an extended slump in shares of industry bellwether Nvidia, which has been hit by revelations surrounding CEO Jensen Huang's romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Helping offset Nvidia's woes was Claude-chatbot-maker Anthropic's filing ahead of a potential blockbuster initial public offering, as well as hopes for de-escalating Middle East tensions that sent oil prices down to their lowest level since August.

Still, short-term U.S. Treasury yields spiked by the most in 19 months, dragging down stocks. A combination of hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data and hawkish comments from some Fed policymakers increased bets that the central bank may lift interest rates more aggressively than initially thought.

Overnight, the AI trade fueled an uptick in equity markets around the world, while bonds sold off in a number of countries, including Japan and Australia. The U.S. bond market will be closed for Veterans Day.

2. CoreWeave's upbeat outlook

Along with concerns that Democratic lawmakers will use their post-midterm influence to slow AI development, doubts have long swirled around the financial stability of an industry known for massive infrastructure spending plans.

CoreWeave's shares have tumbled in recent weeks against this backdrop, shedding more than 40% of their value over the past month alone. The Nvidia-backed company has accrued roughly $50 billion in debt, turning it into a poster child for the heavy borrowing being tapped to fund the rapid AI buildout.
